questions.stem: According to the passage, how many teeth did George Washington have left when he was sworn in as president?
options: None
One
Ten
All of his teeth
questions.evidence: When he was sworn in as president, he had only one tooth left.
questions.explanation_ko: 대통령 취임 당시 이빨이 하나만 남아 있었다고 나와 있습니다.

questions.stem: According to the passage, which of the following popular stories about George Washington is actually confirmed as TRUE?
options: He had wooden teeth
He chopped down a cherry tree and admitted it by saying 'I cannot tell a lie'
He wore dentures made partly from hippopotamus ivory
He never told a lie in his life
questions.evidence: But he did wear dentures. They were made, in part, from hippopotamus ivory.
questions.explanation_ko: 나무 이빨과 벚나무 일화는 사실이 아니라고 나와 있지만, 하마 상아로 만든 틀니를 착용한 것은 사실이라고 나와 있습니다.

questions.stem: What can be inferred from Washington's regret that he had not done more to end slavery and his will freeing his slaves?
options: Washington supported slavery throughout his entire life without any change in view.
Washington's opposition to slavery grew over his life, even though he had been a slaveholder for most of it.
Washington freed all his slaves immediately after becoming president.
Washington never owned any enslaved people.
questions.evidence: By the end of his life, Washington opposed slavery.
questions.explanation_ko: 생애 말년에 노예제에 반대했다는 내용과 노예 해방을 명시한 유언에서, 그의 견해가 시간이 지나며 더 비판적으로 변했음을 추론할 수 있습니다.

questions.stem: Why does the author quote historian Joseph Ellis saying "Washington went from being a man to a monument"?
options: To show how Washington's public reputation grew larger than life over time
To argue that Washington built actual stone monuments
To criticize modern historians
To explain how the Washington Monument was constructed
questions.evidence: Washington went from being a man to a monument.
questions.explanation_ko: 이 인용문은 워싱턴의 대중적 명성이 시간이 지나며 실제보다 더 크게 부풀려졌음을 보여 주기 위한 것입니다.

questions.stem: In the passage, what does "indispensable" mean in "calls George Washington the 'indispensable man'"?
options: unimportant and easily replaced
extremely important and necessary
wealthy
tall and strong
questions.evidence: calls George Washington the “ indispensable man.”
questions.explanation_ko: indispensable은 매우 중요하고 반드시 필요하다는 뜻입니다.

blanks.sentence_ko: 그는 공직에서 은퇴해 고향으로 돌아가고 싶다고 말했다.
그것은 당시 평균적인 남성보다 머리 하나만큼 더 큰 키였다.
역사학자 조지프 엘리스는 조지 워싱턴의 가장 훌륭한 점 중 하나는 권력을 내려놓을 수 있었다는 것이라고 말한다.

blanks.expression: conspicuously willing to give it up
blanks.sentence_ko: 당신은 워싱턴을 믿을 수 있었습니다, 그가 눈에 띄게 기꺼이 권력을 내려놓으려 했기 때문입니다.

key_points: George Washington, the first U.S. president (1789-1797), was a reluctant leader who wanted to retire after leading the American Revolution and presiding over the Constitutional Convention.
As president, Washington effectively invented the role, establishing the cabinet, national currency, the Supreme Court, and the Department of Foreign Affairs, always working within the Constitution.

Many popular stories about Washington, like wooden teeth or the cherry tree confession, are myths, though it is true he wore dentures partly made of hippopotamus ivory and had only one tooth left by his presidency.

Washington enslaved more than 300 people but came to oppose slavery by the end of his life, leaving a will that ordered his slaves freed after his wife's death, and he is remembered for voluntarily giving up power at the end of his terms.
main_idea: George Washington, though reluctant to serve, effectively invented the U.S. presidency and is remembered as an 'indispensable man' who voluntarily gave up power, despite being a slaveholder for most of his life.
restate_sentence: He was a famous general, who led the American colonists to freedom from British rule.
